newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Satellite subscribers double in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Satellite subscribers double in 1996.

text.p: U.S. Satellite Broadcasting Co said Tuesday that its U.S. subscriber base nearly doubled in 1996 and that December was the best month ever for sales of its 18-inch Digital Satellite System (DSS).
During the quarter, paying subscribers grew by 175,000 to 1,220,000, the company said.

"December was the biggest month ever for DSS sales, said Stanley Hubbard, president and chief executive of U.S. Satellite. "DSS is now in one of every 42 homes in America, and we expect continued strong growth throughout 1997."
The company said more than one million DSS units were sold and installed in U.S. homes in 1996, and the total number of DSS homes now stands at 2.3 million.

"Since its introduction, DSS stands as the fastest selling product in consumer electronics history, and DSS continues to maintain a pace well ahead of other successful products including VCRs, cellular phones and CD players," Hubbard said.

Earlier, U.S. Satellite reported a net loss for the fiscal second quarter of $0.46 a share versus $0.31 last year. The loss was deepened by a $17 million charge for a manufacturer incentive program for DSS. The charge increased the net loss by $12.8 million or $0.15 a share.
